MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The USB hub feels useful because my keyboard receiver, storage devices, and USB Ethernet adapter could compete for ports on my computer.",
    "The USB extension cables fit my interest in arranging and connecting desk equipment, reflected in my cable organizers, cable ties, and earlier extension cable."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The streaming players, tablets, smart speaker, and camera introduce uses I have not been pursuing; buying computer accessories does not mean I currently need those devices.",
    "The Bluetooth speaker does not follow my current listening setup as closely as accessories for my headphones would, especially after my headphone mount purchase.",
    "The memory card resembles earlier purchases, but my latest card was specifically for a Garmin; another card only helps if I have a separate need and it fits the intended device."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "The suggestions seem to treat interest in electronics as a reason to want many kinds of electronic devices, while my recent choices serve specific connectivity and organization needs.",
    "My Kindle and Raspberry Pi purchases seem to have been stretched into interest in tablets and streaming players without a clear connection to what I am doing now."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent Ethernet adapter, Ethernet cables, headphone mount, and cleaning equipment point toward improving and maintaining an existing computer workspace.",
    "Accessories are useful when they solve a remaining problem with equipment I own; a similar item may be unnecessary when a recent purchase already fills that need.",
    "Connections and device compatibility matter: extra USB ports and cable reach have plausible uses, while a memory card requires checking the particular device and storage need."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The suggestions partly recognize my need for computer accessories but too often turn that into a broad interest in unrelated electronic devices."
}
